cues: A player presses combinations of three valves to change tubing length and produce different notes.
Before a performance, the musician oils sticky piston valves so they move quickly during passages.
A sharp breath and steady lip vibration send a bright tone through the flared bell.
During warmups, short repeated notes help build accurate valve changes and clean articulation.
The performer tightens the lips to reach piercing high notes during a ceremonial fanfare.
After playing, the musician empties condensation through a small water key near the valve casing.
A soloist alternates rapid valve combinations while sustaining a clear melody above the ensemble.
The player removes the mouthpiece, wipes it clean, and seats it firmly before the next passage.
